title: Inactive Tracking Projection
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Boolean Turing machine, let $x,y$ be Boolean words, and choose two source configurations $c,c'$ on input $y$, two Boolean tags $b,b'$, two movement-count families $n,n'$, a record word, natural numbers $T,t$, and any tracking configuration $z$ on input $x$. The projections of $z$ into the recorder's tracking slots agree when formed from either recorder layout determined by these choices.
hypotheses_covered: A finite-state Boolean Turing machine M
Source configurations c and c' on input y
A tracking configuration z on input x
replaced: The retained inactive tapes and heads used when relocating a tracking configuration into the recorder depend only on the stored record and clock, so they agree for any two source configurations, tags, and movement counts; source writes and counter updates therefore do not disturb the frame.
